sketches.title: Because Of That
sketches.premise: Tell a small story backwards. One player states what has just happened; the other explains the single event that caused it. The host reports each new cause in a flat voice, as if this was obviously going to happen.
sketches.criterion: A move FOLLOWS if it is one plain event that directly caused the standing event and adds a new fact; it fails by skipping a cause, ending at an ultimate answer such as 'that is just how it was,' undoing or denying the standing event, or bringing in a person or place the scene cannot support.
sketches.move_shape: Start with "Because..." and name one cause, not a reason, feeling, or history lesson. Example: "Because the dog dragged the picnic cloth away."
sketches.first_card: The mayor is standing in a fountain with one wet shoe.

sketches.title: Earlier Than That
sketches.premise: The scene is already in trouble, and each turn must move one step earlier to show how it got there. The host gives a dry note after every answer, kindly pointing out that the past is not improving.
sketches.criterion: A move FOLLOWS if it is one event immediately before and plainly responsible for the standing event, while fitting every earlier fact; skipping a link, reaching a final origin like "someone decided it," undoing a fact, or adding a newcomer the scene could not contain fails.
sketches.move_shape: Write "Earlier, ..." followed by one visible event. Example: "Earlier, the baker left the oven door open."
sketches.first_card: A birthday cake is on the library floor, still wearing its candles.

sketches.title: The Missing Reason
sketches.premise: A puzzling result is on the table. Take turns uncovering one concrete cause at a time, while the host calmly labels each revelation as another poor choice by someone.
sketches.criterion: A move FOLLOWS if it supplies one direct, new cause of the standing fact and keeps the whole chain possible; a skipped step, a stopping answer such as luck or magic, a reversal that removes a fact, or a person, object, or place not established in the scene fails.
sketches.move_shape: Use "This happened because..." and name an event that could be seen or heard. Example: "This happened because the cat pulled the ribbon through the keyhole."
sketches.first_card: The school bell is ringing in the grocery store.

sketches.title: Trace It Back
sketches.premise: Begin with an odd result and trace it back through the small accidents that made it happen. The host supplies deadpan footnotes, especially when a player turns a tiny mistake into a public problem.
sketches.criterion: A move FOLLOWS if it is the next earlier event that caused the standing one, introduces no unsupported newcomer, and preserves all facts; jumping over a needed event, stopping with an uncaused answer, undoing the result, or changing to a separate tale fails.
sketches.move_shape: Say "Right before that, ..." and give one event. Example: "Right before that, the note slid under the door."
sketches.first_card: A violin is hanging from the town clock.

sketches.title: Who Started This
sketches.premise: The last thing in the story is already happening, and players work backward to find the chain of ordinary actions behind it. The host keeps score of the chain, not the player, since the player has already done enough.
sketches.criterion: A move FOLLOWS if it names one immediate cause that fits the entire transcript and leaves a clear earlier question; it fails when it leaps over causes, declares the first cause or ends the story, cancels a standing fact, or imports a newcomer the established scene could not hold.
sketches.move_shape: Begin with "It began when..." only for the next missing event, then stop. Example: "It began when the delivery cart hit the loose gate."
sketches.first_card: The wedding guests are all wearing rain boots.

sketches.title: One Step Before
sketches.premise: Build a backwards chain from a harmless-looking scene, adding exactly one earlier event each turn. The host speaks like a museum guide for bad planning and offers no rescue.
sketches.criterion: A move FOLLOWS if it is one earlier event with a direct, ordinary cause-and-effect link to the standing event and fits every fact already named; a skipped link, a final explanation, an undo, or an unsupported person, object, or location is a fail.
sketches.move_shape: Use "Just before this, ..." and describe one event that caused the current one. Example: "Just before this, the parcel rolled off the counter."
sketches.first_card: A penguin is waiting beside the bus stop with a lunch box.
